text: Two separate fact tables, genuinely sharing the same set of dimensions between them — that's still a real star schema underneath it all, just drawn out as a slightly bigger diagram than you've seen before.

Every single dimension table connects to both fact tables wherever it genuinely applies to each one. Build every one of these relationships as one-to-many, with the dimension firmly sitting on the one side — exactly the same discipline Chapter Four already taught you in full.

FactInternetSales specifically carries three separate date roles at once, but only one single relationship between any two tables can ever be active at the same time. This is genuinely the exact scenario Chapter Six originally used to teach USERELATIONSHIP in the first place — and Lesson 88 puts that same technique directly to work here.

Since this particular relationship actually runs through a whole-number surrogate key rather than the real date column itself, DimDate genuinely has to be explicitly marked as your date table by hand — Power BI's automatic date and time detection simply won't cover this specific relationship correctly on its own.

The model is fully built now, with every relationship correctly in place. Lesson 88 writes the real DAX measures that actually answer every one of Lesson 84's four original requirements, directly and specifically.
